answer: Hide a pearl in the grading queue. Each epoch the network slips in a few planted answers whose quality it already knows, some excellent, some plainly copied. A grader earns weight only by scoring those plants close to truth, so a sybil farm that rubber-stamps everything drains its own reward oasis. Keys can be cheap; judgment across fifty blind plants is not. The weak inlet is the plants themselves: if they share a style, farms learn to spot them, so they must be written fresh and rotated each epoch.
